correctness.rationale: For rate-\(r\) full resets \((X,F)\mapsto(0,0)\), the stationary age is \(\operatorname{Exp}(r)\). Solving the OU stochastic convolution from zero yields conditional variance \(C[hU+g(U)]\) with \(g(u)=2u-3+4e^{-u}-e^{-2u}\). Gaussian fourth-moment conditioning, explicit Laplace integrals of \(g\), \(Ug\) and \(g^2\), and symbolic simplification give the quoted rational \(K\). Its derivative is \(-24P\) divided by a strictly positive denominator, with P degree seven; for h>0 its descending coefficients have one sign change and opposite endpoint signs, so Descartes gives a unique positive root and global maximum. For \(h=0\) the derivative is strictly positive and K increases toward \(57\). Explicit thermal derivative is negative. Python reproduces symbolic identities, 20 numerical integrals, six optimizer cases and three seeded simulations. No finite sample is treated as proof.

value.rationale: Standardized stationary fourth moments are motivated by the exact reset-controlled positional propagator and MSD of the primary 2025 active-OU study. They measure relative rare-excursion weight independent of the shrinking MSD, which cannot be inferred from second moments. The exact classification of all \(h>0\) as having one finite maximizing reset rate versus the \(h=0\) strictly increasing-to-\(57\) boundary is a natural parameter-level phase distinction, and proof requires the nontrivial seven-degree coefficient-sign theorem; it is neither a textbook substitution nor an unmotivated finite-number computation. The claim does not conflate kurtosis optimization with search-time optimization.
